segments.text: A gifted young girl and the only person her misanthropic Onii-chan—a light novel author and the story's protagonist—has ever truly opened his heart to.
Too intelligent for her own good, with unnaturally pale skin and snow-white hair, she has always stood out. Unable to fit in at school, she withdrew from the world, much like Onii-chan.
More closely than anyone else, she quietly watches over him as he begins his career as a light novel author.
She wants Onii-chan she loves more than anyone to become successful. And yet, the thought of him becoming popular also fills her with sadness.

Deep down, she believes they'll remain together until the very end, no matter what happens. Because of that, she sees the quiet life they share as "an extraordinarily slow form of suicide"—a thought so calm and matter-of-fact that it is all the more unsettling.
From official profile
Onii-chan—better known as "Hasuya."

A college student with a permanent scowl and practically no friends. He barely showed up to class to begin with, and ever since he started working the night shift at a convenience store, he goes even less.

Ever since he was born, he's been able to perceive the colors of people's emotions and hear the thoughts running through their minds. Once, he used that ability against someone he hated and ended up driving them to a suicide attempt.
The guilt still haunts him, but even so... he can't bring himself to like people.
Because he can read what's inside them, he trusts almost no one. The only person he's ever truly opened his heart to is his little sister.
Just when it seemed like his future was headed nowhere, the light novel he submitted to a contest unexpectedly won an award, launching his career as a professional author.
It should have been a happy ending, but the attention around him quickly became tainted with curiosity and jealousy.
For someone as painfully sensitive to other people's emotions as he is, it marked the beginning of a living nightmare.
He's so afraid of other people that he can't help looking down on them in his head. It's a bad habit.
From official profile
A busty, quintessential subculture college girl.
Determined to elevate her own social value, she eagerly starts DMing the protagonist after he debuts as a rookie light novel author, hoping to work her way up to meeting him in person.
She runs a modestly popular social media account.
At first glance, it seems to have grown thanks to her recommendations of obscure novels and cult films—but in reality, she's exceptionally good at weaving carefully chosen selfies into her feed.
She's that kind of calculating little fox.
Naturally, at the otaku club, she's the type who casually ends up sitting on some nerdy guy's lap.

Ever since seeing Girl with a Pearl Earring, she fell in love with the world of fine art. Deep down, she secretly dreams of one day becoming a woman as perfectly complete—as much a work of art—as the girl in that painting.
...Whether that's truly possible, however, is another matter entirely.
From official profile
The protagonist's only real friend—something incredibly rare for someone who dislikes people as much as he does.
That said, they're not especially close.

Their friendship is mostly just inertia from their school days. They don't see each other that often now that they're in college, but since neither of them has really found their place there, neither has had a reason to let the friendship fade away.

To the protagonist, he was simply someone he didn't mind having around. But ever since the protagonist made his debut as a light novel author, his inferiority complex has become painfully obvious, and he's turned into the kind of guy who can't stop making passive-aggressive little remarks.

Watching him desperately throw himself into job hunting, hoping a successful career will somehow restore the balance between them, is honestly a little painful. That sense of inferiority is youth in a nutshell!
He squirms around so much that, every now and then, he genuinely starts to resemble a caterpillar.
From official profile
A senior in the protagonist's literature club, majoring in philosophy.

A pretentious armchair critic who loves throwing around vague phrases like "capturing the essence" or "it lacks narrative depth" to sneer at whatever happens to be popular—or at the protagonist's work.

Before the protagonist made their debut as a commercially published light novel author, he was the undisputed "king" of the club. Now that his position has been threatened, he's desperately trying to protect his status. He mocks the protagonist's writing from every conceivable angle, despite the fact that his own web novel was abandoned almost as soon as he started posting it.

Approach him with caution. Get him talking, and before long he'll launch into something like, "You know, Lacan once said..."—spouting half-digested philosophy in an attempt to sound profound. For all his posturing, though, he's secretly obsessed with cute moe heroines!
That said, compared to most people, he genuinely takes literature seriously, and even those around him have to admit he knows his books.
From official profile
A coworker at the convenience store where the protagonist works the night shift.
He's gotten away with a lot simply because he's good-looking, though it came at the expense of developing much of a brain.
All he wants is an easy life, so he's always chasing easy money.
He's fully aware that he's not very smart. Maybe that's why he has a soft spot for people who seem just as bad at life as he is, and why he can't stand things like bullying.
He takes an interest in the protagonist, sensing how awkwardly they struggle through life, and often goes out of his way to annoy them just for fun.
Taking anything he does seriously is usually a terrible idea, but spending time with him can be surprisingly exciting—and fun.
He's ridiculously fast at stocking shelves.
